For such a site, the summer-solstice altitude is 66°34′ + φ and the winter-solstice altitude is 66°34′ − φ; setting 66°34′ + φ = 86°34′ gives φ = 20°N, and then 66°34′ − 20° = 46°34′, matching the lowest observed value. A latitude of about 20°N lies in the tropical zone, so the climate is most likely tropical monsoon or tropical savanna, characterized by a distinct alternation of wet and dry seasons. Final answer: high temperatures year-round, distinct wet and dry (dry and rainy) seasons, rainy in the wet season and little rain in the dry season.

The v-t graph shows two particles starting from the same point and moving together from rest to 4 m/s during the first 3 s; after t = 3 s, particle A (A) continues to speed up to 6 m/s at t = 5 s, while particle B (B) stays at 4 m/s. Displacement equals the area under the v-t graph. From 0 to 3 s, both particles travel the same distance: \(s_0=\frac12\times3\times4=6\ \text{m}\). From 3 s to 5 s, particle A travels \(s_A'=\frac{(4+6)}{2}\times2=10\ \text{m}\), and particle B travels \(s_B'=4\times2=8\ \text{m}\). Thus the total displacements at t = 5 s are \(s_A=6+10=16\ \text{m}\) and \(s_B=6+8=14\ \text{m}\), so the separation is \(16-14=2\ \text{m}\). Final answer: 2 m.

In Figure A the magnetic field occupies \(0\le x\le d\), point \(M\) is at \((d,0)\), and the \(y\)-axis is the left boundary; Figure B shows the alternating field \(B(t)=B_0\) for \(0<t<T/2\) and \(B(t)=-B_0\) for \(T/2<t<T\), repeating with period \(T\). (1) In \(x<0\) the uniform electric field is along \(+y\). The proton travels horizontally a distance \(\sqrt3\,d\) at speed \(v_0\), so the time is \(t=\sqrt3\,d/v_0\); its vertical displacement is \(d/2\), hence \(\frac12 d=\frac12 a t^2\), giving \(a=v_0^2/(3d)\) and \(v_y=a t=v_0/\sqrt3\). Therefore the speed just inside the field is \(v=\sqrt{v_0^2+v_y^2}=2v_0/\sqrt3\) and the velocity makes an angle \(\theta=\arctan(v_y/v_x)=30^\circ\) above the \(+x\)-axis. (2) Inside the field the radius is \(R=mv/(eB)\). With \(B\) out of the page the proton turns clockwise and returns to the \(y\)-axis after a \(120^\circ\) arc, at time \(t=(120^\circ/360^\circ)(2\pi m/eB)=2\pi m/(3eB)\). For this to occur within \(0<t\le T/2\), \(2\pi m/(3eB)\le T/2\), so the minimum magnetic induction is \(B_{\min}=4\pi m/(3eT)\). (3) To exit at \(M(d,0)\) with the original direction, the simplest one-period path consists of two \(60^\circ\) arcs: a clockwise \(60^\circ\) arc under \(+B_0\) followed by a counterclockwise \(60^\circ\) arc under \(-B_0\). Each chord is horizontal with length \(2R\sin30^\circ=R\), and the total horizontal displacement is \(2R=d\), so \(R=d/2\). Thus \(B_0=mv/(eR)=4mv_0/(\sqrt3\,ed)\). The cyclotron period is \(T_c=2\pi R/v=\pi d\sqrt3/(2v_0)\), and because each \(60^\circ\) arc lasts \(T/2=T_c/6\), the field period is \(T=T_c/3=\pi d\sqrt3/(6v_0)\). Final answer: (1) \(2v_0/\sqrt3\) at \(30^\circ\) above the \(+x\)-axis; (2) \(4\pi m/(3eT)\); (3) \(B_0=4mv_0/(\sqrt3\,ed)\), \(T=\pi d\sqrt3/(6v_0)\).
